items.question: Before engine start, the [STBY INSTR] must be:
items.explanation: The standby instrument must be engaged and checked before start.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-3

items.question: During engine start, which additional setting must be made with the G500H TXi installed?
options: Set G500H TXi parameters (Obstacle, Terrain, DH)
items.explanation: With G500H TXi, obstacle/terrain/DH parameters must be set.

items.question: At power-up, the GTX335R transponder starts in which mode?
items.explanation: GTX335R starts in ALT mode at power-up.

items.question: At power-up with engine OFF, the GTX345R transponder starts in:
items.explanation: With engine OFF, GTX345R initializes in STBY mode.

items.question: If GTN 650Xi fails, what happens to the transponder?
items.explanation: In case of GTN failure, transponder freezes in last selected mode.

items.question: When using NVG or NIGHT mode in cockpit lighting, the selector should be set to:
items.explanation: The selector must be set to NIGHT or NVG for NVIS operations.

items.question: With the optional two-passenger front seat, maximum number of occupants is:
items.explanation: The two-passenger front seat allows for a total of 7 occupants.

items.question: Special attention when operating with two-passenger front seat must be paid to:
items.explanation: CG changes must be considered with two front passengers.

items.question: For hoist operations, the BREEZE BL16600 hoist has a cable length of:
items.explanation: BREEZE BL16600 hoist cable length is 33.5 m (110 ft).

items.question: For hoist operations, the AIR EQUIPMENT 76370 hoist has a cable length of:
items.explanation: AIR EQUIPMENT 76370 hoist cable length is 40 m (130 ft).

items.question: During run-up, after GPS is stable, which GTN page must be pressed?
items.explanation: GTN Transponder page must be pressed during run-up.

items.question: When an aural traffic alert occurs with GTX 345R, pilot action is:
items.explanation: Pilot must visually scan and maneuver if required.

items.question: To silence the aural traffic alert, pilot must press:
items.explanation: TRFC ACK pushbutton silences traffic alerts.

items.question: At engine shutdown, [STBY INSTR] must be:
items.explanation: Standby instrument must be checked and then switched OFF.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-28

items.question: In engine prestart check (pre-MOD 07-20112), before [BATT] the pilot must check:
items.explanation: Before battery ON, the standby horizon must be engaged (pre-MOD).
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-30

items.question: In engine prestart check (post-MOD 07-20112), after [BATT] the pilot must check:
items.explanation: Post-MOD, standby instrument is checked after battery ON.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-31

items.question: In case of cabin smoke from IESI, procedure requires:
items.explanation: Smoke from IESI requires ventilating cabin immediately.

items.question: When DC power is cycled in flight, GOV light will remain ON until:
options: Next engine shutdown and battery OFF on ground
items.explanation: GOV light stays on until next engine shutdown and battery OFF on ground.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-36

items.question: In case of GTN waypoint auto-sequencing error, pilot must:
options: Use Active Leg or Direct To
items.explanation: Correct action is to use Active Leg or Direct To.

items.question: For NVIS operation, cockpit display brightness must be:
items.explanation: Brightness must be adjusted as required for NVIS.

items.question: During engine start, the starter must be released when NG reaches:
items.explanation: Starter is released at approximately 45% NG.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-6

items.question: During engine starting, which item is selected ON once N1 is at or above 67 %?
items.explanation: Section 4.3 Engine starting: when N1 ≥ 67 %, GENE is selected ON (item 7), then the CWP is checked for ENG P, MGB P and HYDR (item 8).

items.question: After engine start, the red GOV light should go out when NG reaches approximately:
items.explanation: The GOV light extinguishes at around 60% NG.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-8

items.question: During run-up, before pulling collective, NR must stabilize at:
items.explanation: Rotor RPM must stabilize at 410 before applying collective.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-9

items.question: In case of VEMD failure of one screen, the pilot must:
items.explanation: Pilot continues with the remaining screen in case of single VEMD failure.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-12

items.question: If both VEMD screens fail, pilot must:
items.explanation: Flight is continued using backup gauges if both VEMD screens fail.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-13

items.question: During flight, HYD TEST switch must be used at:
items.explanation: HYD TEST is only performed on the ground, not in flight.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-15

items.question: Before switching HYD TEST ON, collective must be:
items.explanation: Collective must be fully lowered before performing HYD TEST.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-16

items.question: When using optional dual GPS, initialization must be verified for:
items.explanation: Each GPS unit must be initialized independently.

items.question: When COM 1 is failed, COM 2 may be selected via:
items.explanation: COM 2 can be accessed through the audio control panel.

items.question: After landing, rotor must be stopped with collective:
items.explanation: Collective must be fully down when stopping rotor.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-25

items.question: When rotor brake is applied, NR must be below:
items.explanation: Rotor brake must only be applied when NR is below 170 RPM.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-26

items.question: At shutdown, avionics master must be switched OFF:
options: After generator OFF, before fuel shut-off
items.explanation: Avionics are switched OFF after generator OFF and before fuel shut-off.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-27

items.question: In case of sand/dust landing, pilot must keep NR at:
items.explanation: NR must be maintained at flight idle to prevent engine surge during dust landings.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-29

items.question: For cold weather start, battery must be preheated below:
items.explanation: Below  20  C, the battery must be preheated before start.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-31

items.question: Before engine shutdown, stabilization period at idle must be at least:
items.explanation: A minimum of 1 minute at idle is required before shutdown.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-34

items.question: During engine and rotor shutdown, the cyclic must be placed in:
items.explanation: The cyclic must be centered during engine and rotor shutdown.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-40

items.question: During engine and rotor shutdown, the collective must be:
items.explanation: The collective must be fully down and locked during shutdown.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-41

items.question: At shutdown, twist grip must be set to:
items.explanation: Twist grip must be set to idle before full shutdown.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-42

items.question: Engine oil cooling time before shutdown must be at least:
items.explanation: Engine must be cooled for at least 30 seconds before shutdown.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-43

items.question: In normal conditions, rotor brake may be applied below:
items.explanation: Rotor brake may only be applied below 140 RPM in normal conditions.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-44

items.question: In high wind conditions, rotor brake may be applied below:
items.explanation: Rotor brake may be applied below 170 RPM in high wind conditions.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-45

items.question: Maximum fuel tank capacity is:
items.explanation: The maximum usable fuel tank capacity is 540 liters.
references: RFM H125 Section 4 – Normal Procedures – p. 4-50

items.question: Fuel density used for gauge calibration is:
items.explanation: Fuel gauge is calibrated using a density of 0.79.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-51

items.question: Unusable fuel is reached when the gauge indicates:
items.explanation: Unusable fuel is reached when the gauge reads zero.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-52

items.question: During normal refueling, what must be connected first?
options: Bowser earth cable to electrostatic connector
items.explanation: The earth cable must be connected before fueling to avoid static discharge.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-54

items.question: During refueling, smoking in the safety area is:
items.explanation: Smoking is strictly prohibited during refueling.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-55

items.question: During refueling, the aircraft electrical power supply must be:
items.explanation: Aircraft electrical power must be OFF during refueling.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-56

items.question: Refueling with rotors spinning is allowed only:
options: After approval by authority and per regulations
items.explanation: Refueling with rotors spinning requires approval by authority and adherence to regulations.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-57

items.question: When refueling with rotors spinning, maximum fuel level allowed is:
items.explanation: When refueling with rotors spinning, maximum fuel fill is limited to 95%.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-58

items.question: During preflight in snow/ice, main rotor hub and mast must be checked for:
options: Ice on swashplates and servo controls
items.explanation: Main rotor hub and mast must be free of ice on swashplates and servo controls.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-60

items.question: Tail rotor must be manually rotated before start to:
options: Ensure free rotation and freewheel operation
items.explanation: Tail rotor must be rotated by hand to ensure free rotation and freewheel operation.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-61

items.question: Cabin cover should be removed:
options: Just before engine start to avoid windscreen icing
items.explanation: Cabin cover should be removed just before engine start to avoid icing.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-62

items.question: In cold weather run-up, cyclic may be held 3 04 cm forward for 2 minutes to warm up:
items.explanation: Cyclic forward warms up the spherical thrust bearings.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-63

items.question: During cold weather run-up, yaw pedals must be moved over:
items.explanation: Yaw pedals must be moved over 50% of their travel during cold weather run-up.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-64

items.question: In hydraulic failure training, hydraulic failure safety speed is:
items.explanation: Hydraulic failure training requires maintaining 40 60 KIAS.
references: RFM H125 Section 4   Normal Procedures   p. 4-65

items.question: When an operating limitation is exceeded, what must be entered in the logbook?
options: Only a note that a limit was exceeded
Limit exceeded, duration, extreme value and any additional information for maintenance
Time of day and pilot-in-command only
items.explanation: Section 4.1 requires the logbook entry to state which limit was exceeded, the duration, the extreme value attained and any additional information essential to determine the maintenance action.

items.question: Flight planning for the AS350 B3e must comply with:
options: Section 2, Section 5, Section 6 and applicable Supplements
items.explanation: Section 4.1 states that flight planning must comply with helicopter limitations and performance as given in Sections 2, 5, 6 and the Supplements.

items.question: To ensure proper weight and balance before flight, the pilot must:
options: Check pilot and copilot weights only
Ascertain fuel, oil and payload weights, compute takeoff and landing gross weights and verify CG within Section 2 limits
Ensure payload is below maximum passenger number only
items.explanation: Section 4.1 requires checking fuel, oil and payload, computing takeoff and landing gross weights, and confirming that weight and CG remain within the limitations of Section 2.

items.question: Before beginning the preflight checks, what does Section 4.2 require regarding maintenance?
options: Only scheduled maintenance must be completed
All corrective maintenance required for flightworthiness must have been performed
No maintenance is required if last flight was within 24 hours
Only engine-related maintenance must be done
items.explanation: The preflight check section specifies that all corrective maintenance operations required for flightworthiness must be completed before preflight.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-3

items.question: According to the exterior preflight check, what must be done with picketing items (blanks, covers, blade socks) before flight?
options: Leave them installed until engine start
Remove all picketing items before carrying out the checks
items.explanation: Section 4.2 states that all picketing items such as blanks, covers and blade socks must be removed before performing the exterior preflight checks.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-4

items.question: During the exterior preflight, what must be checked at the engine air intake?
options: Only that the cowl is locked
That it is clean, free of foreign objects, ice or snow accumulations and stagnant water
That the intake is painted white
That the bleed valve is closed
items.explanation: Section 4.2 calls for the engine air intake area to be clean, with no foreign objects, no ice or snow in or around the intake and no stagnant water at the drain hole.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-5

items.question: What hazard is specifically warned about if ice or snow remains in or around the engine air intake?
options: It may reduce lift at low speed
It may be ingested and cause a sudden in-flight engine failure
It may cause temporary VEMD display loss only
It may only increase fuel burn
items.explanation: The preflight section includes a WARNING that ice or snow accumulations remaining in or around the engine air intake may be ingested and can cause a sudden in-flight engine failure.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-5

items.question: During exterior preflight, what must be confirmed regarding the ELT?
items.explanation: Section 4.2 lists the ELT on the exterior check with the requirement to confirm it is in the ARMED position.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-6

items.question: What must be checked regarding loads and objects carried in the cargo compartments during preflight?
options: They are below maximum weight only
items.explanation: The exterior and interior preflight checklists both require that all loads and objects carried are stowed and secured.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-4

items.question: During the interior preflight check, what must be verified about the fire extinguisher?
options: That it is removed from its bracket
That it is secured and checked
That it is stowed in the baggage compartment
items.explanation: The interior preflight checklist requires the cabin fire extinguisher to be secured and checked.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.2   Preflight Check   p. 4-7

items.question: During engine prestart check, how must the rotor brake be set before engine start?
items.explanation: Section 4.3 prestart item 1 requires the rotor brake to be RELEASE, fully forward before engine start.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-3

items.question: In the engine prestart check, what is the correct position of the fuel shut-off lever?
options: FORWARD, with plastic guard in place
items.explanation: The prestart checklist in Section 4.3 calls for the fuel shut-off lever to be FORWARD, with its plastic guard in place.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-3

items.question: When performing the [W/LT TST] during engine prestart, what torque indication must be observed on the VEMD?
options: TRQ briefly indicates 50% then returns to 0%
TRQ indicates 100% for about 2 seconds then returns to 0%
TRQ remains at 0% throughout the test
TRQ cycles between 0% and 100% for 10 seconds
items.explanation: Section 4.3 specifies that during [W/LT TST] the torque indication must go to 100% for about 2 seconds and then return to 0%.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-3

items.question: During the VEMD check at the end of the engine prestart check, which combination of indications is required?
options: Hydraulic pressure 2000 psi, NR tape visible, TOT at zero
3-data page shows no messages, vehicle page shows no messages, battery voltage > 22 V, correct fuel quantity and bleed valve open
Only the FLI page is displayed with TOT on scale
Fuel flow page displayed with fuel flow at zero and GOV light ON
items.explanation: Section 4.3 prestart item 14 requires the VEMD 3-data and vehicle pages to show no messages, battery voltage to be above 22 V, fuel quantity to be checked and the bleed valve to be open.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-4

items.question: During engine start, which set of parameters must be monitored according to Section 4.3?
options: Only torque, NR and hydraulic pressure
N1 increases, TOT remains within limits, rotor turns when N1 is ≤ 25% and engine oil pressure increases
items.explanation: Engine start item 6 in Section 4.3 lists these four indications: N1 increasing, TOT staying below its limits, rotor turning at N1 ≤ 25 % and engine oil pressure increasing.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-6

items.question: When N1 reaches at least 67% during engine start, which CWP lights must be checked?
items.explanation: Section 4.3 engine starting item 8 calls for checking that ENG P, MGB P and HYDR are indicated on the CWP when N1 is at or above 67%.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-6

items.question: How must the [FUEL P]/[FUEL PUMP] switch be used in the standard engine start sequence?
options: Left OFF during the entire start to avoid overpressure
Set to ON before engine start, then set to OFF after start while checking that the FUEL P caution appears
Pulsed ON and OFF every 5 seconds during the start
Used only in case of hot start
items.explanation: Section 4.3 engine starting items 2 and 10 require [FUEL P]/[FUEL PUMP] ON before start, then OFF after start with the FUEL P caution checked.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-6

items.question: During the hydraulic cut-off test in the run-up check, what HYDR warning timing is acceptable after returning the hydraulic cut-off switch to ON?
options: HYDR light remains on for at least 10 seconds
items.explanation: Section 4.3 run-up check states that HYDR must come back on the CWP after 3 to 4 seconds; if the time is reduced to 1 second or greater than 4 seconds, maintenance action is required.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-7

items.question: During the [HORN] check in the run-up, when is the audio warning required to be ON and OFF?
options: ON for NR ≤ 320 rpm and OFF above 320 rpm
ON for NR ≤ 340 rpm and OFF above 340 rpm
ON for NR ≤ 360 rpm and OFF for NR above 360 rpm
ON only at nominal rotor speed (394 rpm)
items.explanation: Section 4.3 run-up check specifies that during the horn test the audio warning must be ON for NR at or below 360 rpm and OFF for NR above 360 rpm.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-8

items.question: According to the cranking procedure in Section 4.3, why must the engine not be cranked with the emergency fuel shutoff valve closed?
options: It may discharge the battery too quickly
It may damage the engine high pressure fuel pump
It may cause the GOV light to remain on for the rest of the flight
It may overheat the starter-generator cooling fan
items.explanation: The cranking CAUTION in Section 4.3 warns that cranking with the emergency fuel shutoff valve closed can damage the engine high pressure fuel pump.
references: RFM H125 Section 4.3 – Start Up – p. 4-9

items.question: Before takeoff, how must the doors be configured according to the checklist?
options: Keep all doors open and unsecured for ventilation
Keep all doors closed and latched or sliding doors open and locked
Keep only cockpit doors closed, cabin doors may remain unlocked
Keep all doors partially open for quick egress
items.explanation: Section 4.4 before takeoff requires that doors are either closed and latched or that sliding doors are open and locked in the open position.

items.question: What must be verified about engine and system parameters before takeoff?
options: All parameters are in the red range to ensure maximum power
Temperatures and pressures are within normal ranges and all CWP and overhead lights are out
Only hydraulic pressure and fuel quantity are within limits
Only VEMD pages are displayed without regard to limits
items.explanation: The before takeoff check in Section 4.4 calls for all temperatures and pressures in the normal ranges with no CWP or overhead warning/caution lights remaining on.

items.question: At what approximate height should the helicopter be held in hover before initiating forward takeoff?
items.explanation: The takeoff procedure in Section 4.4 specifies a hover at about 5 ft (HIGE) to check engine and mechanical parameters before accelerating.

items.question: According to the standard takeoff path, which combination of height and IAS must be achieved as the helicopter leaves the hover?
items.explanation: Section 4.4 states that after hovering and accelerating with HIGE power, the helicopter should pass 40 ft at about 50 kt IAS while avoiding the shaded HV diagram area.

items.question: What is the main reason for following the recommended takeoff profile given in Section 4.4?
options: To minimize cabin noise for passengers
To avoid the shaded area of the height-velocity diagram while checking engine parameters
To reach cruise altitude as fast as possible regardless of limits
To keep rotor RPM intentionally low during takeoff
items.explanation: The takeoff profile is designed to keep the helicopter outside the shaded region of the height-velocity diagram while allowing verification of engine and mechanical parameters.

items.question: What indicated airspeed gives best rate of climb at sea level according to Section 4.5?
items.explanation: Section 4.5 specifies a best rate of climb speed of about 65 kt at sea level, decreasing with altitude.

items.question: How is fast cruise speed defined in the Normal Procedures section?
options: The highest IAS that keeps the FLI in the green range
The IAS corresponding to the first yellow limitation on the FLI
The IAS that gives minimum fuel consumption
items.explanation: Section 4.5 defines fast cruise as flight at the first yellow limitation on the FLI, respecting all limits.

items.question: What limitation is given for hover turns in the Normal Procedures?
options: Perform hover turns only into the wind
Avoid hover turns faster than one full rotation in 6 seconds
Avoid hover turns slower than one full rotation in 6 seconds
items.explanation: Section 4.5 recommends avoiding hover turns faster than one full rotation in 6 seconds to limit loads on the tail rotor system.

items.question: How should the approach be flown according to Section 4.5?
options: Maintain VNE to short final and then reduce to hover in the last 10 ft
Begin the approach at best rate of climb speed and reduce IAS near 100 ft to arrive in hover at about 5 ft
Fly the entire approach at 40 kt IAS regardless of wind
Descend vertically from 200 ft with collective only
items.explanation: The approach procedure describes starting the approach at the recommended climb/cruise speed and reducing IAS near 100 ft to arrive in a hover at about 5 ft.

items.question: During a hover landing, how should the collective be used according to the Normal Procedures?
options: Lower the collective abruptly to minimize ground run
Gradually lower the collective to touchdown and then continue the reduction to full down
Hold collective fixed until the skids touch and then raise it
Increase collective slightly during touchdown to soften the landing
items.explanation: Section 4.5 landing procedure specifies that in hover landing the pilot should gradually lower the collective to touchdown and then continue to full down.

items.question: According to the engine and rotor shutdown procedure, what is the required position of the cyclic before shutdown?
items.explanation: Section 4.6 states that the cyclic must be placed in the CENTER position as the first item of the engine and rotor shutdown checklist.

RFM H125 Section 4.6 – Engine and Rotor Shutdown

items.question: How long must the engine be allowed to cool before continuing with shutdown items?
items.explanation: Item 4 of the engine and rotor shutdown checklist requires a 30-second engine oil cooling period before proceeding.

items.question: At what rotor speed NR must the [GENE] switch be turned OFF in normal and high wind conditions?
options: NR ≤ 140 rpm in normal conditions and NR ≤ 170 rpm in high wind conditions
NR ≤ 170 rpm in normal conditions and NR ≤ 140 rpm in high wind conditions
items.explanation: Item 8 of Section 4.6 specifies that [GENE] must be turned OFF at NR ≤ 170 rpm in high wind conditions or NR ≤ 140 rpm in normal conditions.

items.question: What is the purpose of the yaw load compensator check during shutdown?
options: To verify that the left pedal can be fully depressed with high force
To confirm that the right pedal moves forward without pilot input or can be moved forward with low force
To verify that the pedals are locked in a fixed position
items.explanation: Section 4.6 requires a yaw load compensator check where the right pedal moves forward without input or can be moved forward with low force before activating [ACCU TST].
items.manual: RFM H125 Section 4.6 – Engine and Rotor Shutdown
references: RFM H125 Section 4.6 – Engine and Rotor Shutdown – p. 4-17
RFM H125 Section 4.6 – Engine and Rotor Shutdown

items.question: After shutdown and before leaving the helicopter, what VEMD data must be checked on the Flight Report page?
options: Only fuel remaining and outside air temperature
Operating time, usage counter, N1 and N2 cycles and any FAILURE or OVERLIMIT messages
Only accumulated flight time since last maintenance
Only the last displayed FLI values
items.explanation: Section 4.6 item 12 calls for checking operating time, usage counter, N1 and N2 cycles and any FAILURE or OVERLIMIT messages on the VEMD Flight Report page.

items.question: What is the maximum fuel tank capacity given in Section 4.7?
items.explanation: Section 4.7 states that the maximum fuel tank capacity is 540 liters (142.7 US gal).
items.manual: RFM H125 Section 4.7 – Miscellaneous Procedures and Data
references: RFM H125 Section 4.7 – Miscellaneous Procedures and Data – p. 4-18
RFM H125 Section 4.7 – Miscellaneous Procedures and Data
items.source: RFM H125 Section 4.7 – Miscellaneous Procedures and Data

items.question: When is the unusable fuel quantity reached according to the fuel gauge note in Section 4.7?
options: When 10 liters remain in the tank
When the FUEL caution light comes on
When zero is indicated on the fuel gauge
When the fuel flow indicator shows zero
items.explanation: Note 1 under the fuel gauge in Section 4.7 specifies that the unusable fuel quantity is reached when zero is indicated on the fuel gauge.

items.question: Which fuel density is used as the basis for the fuel quantity and fuel flow indications in Section 4.7?
items.explanation: Note 2 in Section 4.7 states that fuel quantity in kg and fuel flow in kg/h are based on a fuel density of 0.79.

items.question: In high wind operation (wind above 30 kt), how must the helicopter be parked according to Section 4.8?
options: With the tail into the wind and no rotor brake applied
Head into the wind with rotor brake applied and one blade at the 12 o'clock position and blade socks fitted
Across the wind with collective full up
Any heading as long as the parking brake is set
items.explanation: Section 4.8 high wind operation recommends parking the helicopter head into the wind, maintaining rotor brake applied with one blade at 12 o'clock and keeping blade socks fitted until start up.

items.question: From the high wind operation section, above what wind speed must the helicopter be tied down?
items.explanation: Section 4.8 specifies that for wind above 40 kt the helicopter must be tied down.
